sanskrit: vāyuvego vāyubalo vāyuhā vāyumaṇḍalaḥ vāyujvālo vāyuretā vāyucakraś ca vīryavān evam ete samutpannā marutāṃ janayiṣṇavaḥ
english: Vāyuvega and Vāyubala, Vāyuha and Vāyumaṇḍala, Vāyujvāla, Vāyuretas, and the valiant Vāyucakra — thus were these born, the begetters of the hosts of the Maruts.

sanskrit: idam anyac ca rājendra śṛṇv āścaryataraṃ bhuvi maharṣeś caritaṃ yādṛk triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
english: And hear now, O lord of kings, another wonder more marvellous still upon this earth — such a deed of that great seer as is renowned throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: purā maṅkaṇakaḥ siddhaḥ kuśāgreṇeti naḥ śrutam kṣataḥ kila kare rājaṃs tasya śākaraso 'sravat sa vi śākarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣāviṣṭaḥ pranṛttavān
english: Of old, Maṅkaṇaka the perfected one — so we have heard — wounded his hand upon the tip of a kuśa-blade, O king, and from it flowed a sap like vegetable juice; and beholding that sap, he was seized with joy and fell to dancing.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin pranṛtte vai sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat pranṛttam ubhayaṃ vīra tejasā tasya mohitam
english: Then as he danced, all that was unmoving and all that moves — both alike, O hero — fell to dancing, bewildered by the force of his power.

sanskrit: brahmādibhiḥ surai rājann ṛṣibhiś ca tapodhanaiḥ vijñapto vai mahādeva ṛṣer arthe narādhipa nāyaṃ nṛtyed yathā deva tathā tvaṃ kartum arhasi
english: Then the gods led by Brahmā, O king, and the seers rich in penance besought Mahādeva on the seer's behalf, O lord of men: 'Bring it to pass, O god, that this one dance no longer.'

sanskrit: tato devo muniṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣāviṣṭam atīva ha surāṇāṃ hitakāmārthaṃ mahādevo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Then the god, seeing the sage utterly transported with joy, Mahādeva, desiring the welfare of the gods, addressed him thus:

sanskrit: bho bho brāhmaṇa dharmajña kimarthaṃ narinartsi vai harṣasthānaṃ kimarthaṃ vai tavedaṃ munisattama tapasvino dharmapathe sthitasya dvijasattama
english: 'Ho there, Brāhmaṇa, knower of dharma, why do you dance on so? What cause for joy is this of yours, O best of sages — for one given to penance and set upon the path of dharma, O best of the twice-born?'

sanskrit: ṛṣir uvāca kiṃ na paśyasi me brahman karāc chākarasaṃ srutam yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai pranṛtto 'haṃ harṣeṇa mahatā vibho
english: The seer said: 'Do you not see, O brahman, the sap that has flowed from my hand? Beholding it I fell to dancing in great joy, O mighty one.'

sanskrit: taṃ prahasyābravīd devo muniṃ rāgeṇa mohitam ahaṃ na vismayaṃ vipra gacchāmīti prapaśya mām
english: Laughing, the god said to the sage thus bewildered by passion: 'I, O brahman, am not moved to wonder by such a thing — look upon me.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā muniśreṣṭhaṃ mahādevena dhīmatā aṅgulyagreṇa rājendra svāṅguṣṭhas tāḍito 'bhavat
english: Having so spoken to the best of sages, the wise Mahādeva, O lord of kings, struck his own thumb with the tip of his finger.

sanskrit: tato bhasma kṣatād rājan nirgataṃ himasaṃnibham tad dṛṣṭvā vrīḍito rājan sa muniḥ pādayor gataḥ
english: Then from the cut, O king, came forth ash white as snow; and seeing it, O king, the sage was abashed and fell at his feet.

sanskrit: ṛṣir uvāca nānyaṃ devād ahaṃ manye rudrāt parataraṃ mahat surāsurasya jagato gatis tvam asi śūladhṛk
english: The seer said: 'I deem none greater, none mightier, than the god Rudra; you, wielder of the trident, are the refuge of the world of gods and demons alike.'

sanskrit: tvayā sṛṣṭam idaṃ viśvaṃ vadantīha manīṣiṇaḥ tvām eva sarvaṃ viśati punar eva yugakṣaye
english: 'By you was this universe created, so the wise declare here; and into you alone does all enter again at the ending of the age.'

sanskrit: devair api na śakyas tvaṃ parijñātuṃ kuto mayā tvayi sarve sma dṛśyante surā brahmādayo 'nagha
english: 'Not even by the gods can you be fully known — how then by me? In you are all the gods beheld, beginning with Brahmā, O sinless one.'

sanskrit: sarvas tvam asi devānāṃ kartā kārayitā ca ha tvatprasādāt surāḥ sarve modantīhākutobhayāḥ
english: 'You are all things; you are of the gods the doer and the cause of doing; by your grace all the gods rejoice here, freed from every fear.'

sanskrit: evaṃ stutvā mahādevaṃ sa ṛṣiḥ praṇato 'bravīt bhagavaṃs tvatprasādād vai tapo me na kṣared iti
english: Having thus praised Mahādeva, the seer bowed low and said: 'O Lord, by your grace may my penance never wane.'

sanskrit: tato devaḥ prītamanās tam ṛṣiṃ punar abravīt tapas te vardhatāṃ vipra matprasādāt sahasradhā āśrame ceha vatsyāmi tvayā sārdham ahaṃ sadā
english: Then the god, well pleased in heart, spoke again to that seer: 'May your penance increase a thousandfold by my grace, O brahman; and here in this hermitage I shall ever dwell together with you.'

sanskrit: saptasārasvate cāsmin yo mām arciṣyate naraḥ na tasya durlabhaṃ kiṃ cid bhaviteha paratra ca sārasvataṃ ca lokaṃ te gamiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'And whatever man shall worship me here at this Seven-Sarasvatī, nothing shall be hard for him to win, in this world or the next; and they shall go to the Sārasvata world, of this there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: etan maṅkaṇakasyāpi caritaṃ bhūritejasaḥ sa hi putraḥ sajanyāyām utpanno mātariśvanā
english: Such was the deed of Maṅkaṇaka of abundant splendour; for he was a son begotten upon Sajanyā by Mātariśvan, the Wind.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uṣitvā tatra rāmas tu saṃpūjyāśramavāsinaḥ tathā maṅkaṇake prītiṃ śubhāṃ cakre halāyudhaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having dwelt there and honoured the dwellers of the hermitage, Rāma the plough-wielder showed too his gracious favour toward Maṅkaṇaka.

sanskrit: dattvā dānaṃ dvijātibhyo rajanīṃ tām upoṣya ca pūjito munisaṃghaiś ca prātar utthāya lāṅgalī
english: Having given gifts to the twice-born and passed that night in fasting, honoured by the throngs of sages, the plough-bearer rose at dawn.

sanskrit: anujñāpya munīn sarvān spṛṣṭvā toyaṃ ca bhārata prayayau tvarito rāmas tīrthahetor mahābalaḥ
english: Having taken leave of all the sages and touched water, O Bhārata, mighty Rāma set forth in haste for the sake of the sacred fords.

sanskrit: tata auśanasaṃ tīrtham ājagāma halāyudhaḥ kapālamocanaṃ nāma yatra mukto mahāmuniḥ
english: Then the plough-wielder came to the ford of Uśanas, called Kapālamocana, the Skull-Release, where the great sage was set free.

sanskrit: mahatā śirasā rājan grastajaṅgho mahodaraḥ rākṣasasya mahārāja rāmakṣiptasya vai purā
english: There, O king, Mahodara had had his leg gripped by a great head — the head of a rākṣasa hurled of old by Rāma, O mighty monarch.

sanskrit: tatra pūrvaṃ tapas taptaṃ kāvyena sumahātmanā yatrāsya nītir akhilā prādurbhūtā mahātmanaḥ tatrasthaś cintayām āsa daityadānavavigraham
english: There of old the great-souled Kāvya practised penance, and there the whole of his statecraft came forth for that high-souled one; abiding there he pondered the warfare of the Daityas and Dānavas.

sanskrit: tat prāpya ca balo rājaṃs tīrthapravaram uttamam vidhivad dhi dadau vittaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām
english: And having reached that most excellent of fords, O king, Bala duly bestowed wealth upon the great-souled Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kapālamocanaṃ brahman kathaṃ yatra mahāmuniḥ muktaḥ kathaṃ cāsya śiro lagnaṃ kena ca hetunā
english: Janamejaya said: How, O brahman, came it to be the Skull-Release, where the great sage was freed? How did the head cleave to him, and for what cause?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca purā vai daṇḍakāraṇye rāghaveṇa mahātmanā vasatā rājaśārdūla rākṣasās tatra hiṃsitāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Of old, in the Daṇḍaka forest, by the great-souled Rāghava dwelling there, O tiger among kings, were the rākṣasas slain.

sanskrit: janasthāne śiraś chinnaṃ rākṣasasya durātmanaḥ kṣureṇa śitadhāreṇa tat papāta mahāvane
english: At Janasthāna the head of an evil-souled rākṣasa was severed with a keen-edged shaft, and it fell within the great forest.

sanskrit: mahodarasya tal lagnaṃ jaṅghāyāṃ vai yadṛcchayā vane vicarato rājann asthi bhittvāsphurat tadā
english: That head, by chance, fastened upon the shin of Mahodara as he wandered in the forest, O king, piercing the bone and there it stuck fast.

sanskrit: sa tena lagnena tadā dvijātir na śaśāka ha abhigantuṃ mahāprājñas tīrthāny āyatanāni ca
english: With that thing clinging to him the twice-born one, wise though he was, could no longer make his way to the fords and holy places.

sanskrit: sa pūtinā visravatā vedanārto mahāmuniḥ jagāma sarvatīrthāni pṛthivyām iti naḥ śrutam
english: Tormented with pain by the foul stuff that oozed from it, the great sage went, so we have heard, to all the sacred fords upon the earth.

sanskrit: sa gatvā saritaḥ sarvāḥ samudrāṃś ca mahātapāḥ kathayām āsa tat sarvam ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: Having gone to all the rivers and to the seas, that great ascetic told all this to the seers of purified souls.

sanskrit: āplutaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu na ca mokṣam avāptavān sa tu śuśrāva viprendro munīnāṃ vacanaṃ mahat
english: Bathing in all the fords, he yet won no release; but that lord of brahmans heard a weighty word of the sages.

sanskrit: sarasvatyās tīrthavaraṃ khyātam auśanasaṃ tadā sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ siddhakṣetram anuttamam
english: That on the Sarasvatī there was a renowned excellent ford of Uśanas, dispeller of all sins, an unsurpassed field of the perfected ones.

sanskrit: sa tu gatvā tatas tatra tīrtham auśanasaṃ dvijaḥ tata auśanase tīrthe tasyopaspṛśatas tadā tacchiraś caraṇaṃ muktvā papātāntarjale tadā
english: And the twice-born one, going thither to the ford of Uśanas, as he touched the water at the ford of Uśanas, that head let go his foot and fell down into the depths of the water.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa virujo rājan pūtātmā vītakalmaṣaḥ ājagāmāśramaṃ prītaḥ kṛtakṛtyo mahodaraḥ
english: Then Mahodara, freed of pain, O king, his soul made pure and his stain gone, came back glad to his hermitage, his purpose fulfilled.

sanskrit: so 'tha gatvāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ vipramukto mahātapāḥ kathayām āsa tat sarvam ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: And the great ascetic, set free and come to the holy hermitage, told all this to the seers of purified souls.

sanskrit: te śrutvā vacanaṃ tasya tatas tīrthasya mānada kapālamocanam iti nāma cakruḥ samāgatāḥ
english: Hearing his words, O giver of honour, the assembled sages gave to that ford the name Kapālamocana, the Skull-Release.

sanskrit: tatra dattvā bahūn dāyān viprān saṃpūjya mādhavaḥ jagāma vṛṣṇipravaro ruṣaṅgorāśramaṃ tadā
english: There Mādhava, the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis, having given many gifts and honoured the brahmans, went then to the hermitage of Ruṣaṅgu.

sanskrit: yatra taptaṃ tapo ghoram ārṣṭiṣeṇena bhārata brāhmaṇyaṃ labdhavāṃs tatra viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
english: Where Ārṣṭiṣeṇa had practised dread penance, O Bhārata, and where the great sage Viśvāmitra had won the estate of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tato haladharaḥ śrīmān brāhmaṇaiḥ parivāritaḥ jagāma yatra rājendra ruṣaṅgus tanum atyajat
english: Thence the glorious plough-bearer, surrounded by brahmans, went, O lord of kings, to the place where Ruṣaṅgu had laid down his body.

sanskrit: ruṣaṅgur brāhmaṇo vṛddhas taponityaś ca bhārata dehanyāse kṛtamanā vicintya bahudhā bahu
english: Ruṣaṅgu, an aged brāhmaṇa ever devoted to penance, O Bhārata, set his mind upon laying down his body, having pondered the matter long and in many ways.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvān upādāya tanayān vai mahātapāḥ ruṣaṅgur abravīt tatra nayadhvaṃ mā pṛthūdakam
english: Then the great ascetic Ruṣaṅgu, gathering all his sons, said to them: 'Lead me to Pṛthūdaka.'

sanskrit: vijñāyātītavayasaṃ ruṣaṅguṃ te tapodhanāḥ taṃ vai tīrtham upāninyuḥ sarasvatyās tapodhanam
english: Knowing Ruṣaṅgu, rich in penance, to be far advanced in years, those ascetics led him to that ford of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ putrais tadā dhīmān ānīto vai sarasvatīm puṇyāṃ tīrthaśatopetāṃ viprasaṃghair niṣevitām
english: Brought then by his sons, that wise one came to the Sarasvatī, holy, endowed with a hundred fords, frequented by throngs of brahmans.

sanskrit: sa tatra vidhinā rājann āplutaḥ sumahātapāḥ jñātvā tīrthaguṇāṃś caiva prāhedam ṛṣisattamaḥ suprītaḥ puruṣavyāghra sarvān putrān upāsataḥ
english: There, O king, having bathed according to rite, that great ascetic, knowing the virtues of the ford, the best of seers, well pleased, O tiger among men, spoke thus to all his sons who attended upon him:

sanskrit: sarasvaty uttare tīre yas tyajed ātmanas tanum pṛthūdake japyaparo nainaṃ śvomaraṇaṃ tapet
english: 'Whoever on the northern bank of the Sarasvatī, at Pṛthūdaka, intent upon prayer, lays down his body — him the morrow's death shall not afflict.'

sanskrit: tatrāplutya sa dharmātmā upaspṛśya halāyudhaḥ dattvā caiva bahūn dāyān viprāṇāṃ vipravatsalaḥ
english: There the righteous plough-bearer bathed and touched the water, and gave many gifts, fond as he was of the brahmans.

sanskrit: sasarja yatra bhagavāṃl lokāṃl lokapitāmahaḥ yatrārṣṭiṣeṇaḥ kauravya brāhmaṇyaṃ saṃśitavrataḥ tapasā mahatā rājan prāptavān ṛṣisattamaḥ
english: Where the Lord, the Grandsire of the worlds, brought forth the worlds; where, O Kaurava, Ārṣṭiṣeṇa of firm vows, the best of seers, attained brāhmaṇa-hood through mighty penance, O king.

sanskrit: sindhudvīpaś ca rājarṣir devāpiś ca mahātapāḥ brāhmaṇyaṃ labdhavān yatra viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ mahātapasvī bhagavān ugratejā mahātapāḥ
english: And where the royal seer Sindhudvīpa, and Devāpi of great penance, and the great sage Viśvāmitra — that mighty ascetic, the lord of fierce splendour and great penance — won brāhmaṇa-hood.

sanskrit: tatrājagāma balavān balabhadraḥ pratāpavān
english: Thither came the mighty and majestic Balabhadra.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca katham ārṣṭiṣeṇo bhagavān vipulaṃ taptavāṃs tapaḥ sindhudvīpaḥ kathaṃ cāpi brāhmaṇyaṃ labdhavāṃs tadā
english: Janamejaya said: How did the lord Ārṣṭiṣeṇa practise his vast penance, and how too did Sindhudvīpa then win brāhmaṇa-hood?

sanskrit: devāpiś ca kathaṃ brahman viśvāmitraś ca sattama tan mamācakṣva bhagavan paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: And how Devāpi, O brahman, and how Viśvāmitra, O best of men? Tell me this, O lord, for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca purā kṛtayuge rājann ārṣṭiṣeṇo dvijottamaḥ vasan gurukule nityaṃ nityam adhyayane rataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Of old, in the Kṛta age, O king, Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, best of the twice-born, dwelling ever in his teacher's house, was ever devoted to study.

sanskrit: tasya rājan gurukule vasato nityam eva ha samāptiṃ nāgamad vidyā nāpi vedā viśāṃ pate
english: Yet for him, O king, dwelling ever in his teacher's house, his learning came to no completion, nor did the Vedas, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: sa nirviṇṇas tato rājaṃs tapas tepe mahātapāḥ tato vai tapasā tena prāpya vedān anuttamān
english: Then, grown weary, O king, that great ascetic practised penance; and by that penance he won the supreme Vedas.

sanskrit: sa vidvān vedayuktaś ca siddhaś cāpy ṛṣisattamaḥ tatra tīrthe varān prādāt trīn eva sumahātapāḥ
english: Learned and endowed with the Vedas and perfected, the best of seers, that great ascetic bestowed three boons there at the ford.

sanskrit: asmiṃs tīrthe mahānadyā adyaprabhṛti mānavaḥ āpluto vājimedhasya phalaṃ prāpnoti puṣkalam
english: 'At this ford of the great river, from this day forth, the man who bathes shall win the abundant fruit of the horse-sacrifice.'

sanskrit: adyaprabhṛti naivātra bhayaṃ vyālād bhaviṣyati api cālpena yatnena phalaṃ prāpsyati puṣkalam
english: 'From this day forth there shall be here no fear from beasts of prey, and even with little effort one shall win abundant fruit.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā jagāma tridivaṃ muniḥ evaṃ siddhaḥ sa bhagavān ārṣṭiṣeṇaḥ pratāpavān
english: Having so spoken, the sage of great splendour went to the third heaven; thus did the majestic lord Ārṣṭiṣeṇa attain perfection.

sanskrit: tasminn eva tadā tīrthe sindhudvīpaḥ pratāpavān devāpiś ca mahārāja brāhmaṇyaṃ prāpatur mahat
english: At that very ford then the majestic Sindhudvīpa, and Devāpi, O mighty king, attained the high estate of brāhmaṇa-hood.

sanskrit: tathā ca kauśikas tāta taponityo jitendriyaḥ tapasā vai sutaptena brāhmaṇatvam avāptavān
english: And likewise Kauśika, my son, ever devoted to penance, his senses subdued, attained brāhmaṇa-hood through well-practised penance.

sanskrit: gādhir nāma mahān āsīt kṣatriyaḥ prathito bhuvi tasya putro 'bhavad rājan viśvāmitraḥ pratāpavān
english: There was a great kṣatriya named Gādhi, renowned upon the earth; his son, O king, was the majestic Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: sa rājā kauśikas tāta mahāyogy abhavat kila sa putram abhiṣicyātha viśvāmitraṃ mahātapāḥ
english: That king Kauśika, my son, became a great yogin, it is said; and the great ascetic, having consecrated his son Viśvāmitra,

sanskrit: dehanyāse manaś cakre tam ūcuḥ praṇatāḥ prajāḥ na gantavyaṃ mahāprājña trāhi cāsmān mahābhayāt
english: set his mind upon laying down his body; but his subjects, bowing low, said to him: 'You must not go, O wise one; save us from this great peril.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca tato gādhiḥ prajās tadā viśvasya jagato goptā bhaviṣyati suto mama
english: Thus addressed, Gādhi then answered his subjects: 'My son shall be the protector of the whole world.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā tu tato gādhir viśvāmitraṃ niveśya ca jagāma tridivaṃ rājan viśvāmitro 'bhavan nṛpaḥ na ca śaknoti pṛthivīṃ yatnavān api rakṣitum
english: Having so spoken, Gādhi, having established Viśvāmitra in his place, went to the third heaven, O king; and Viśvāmitra became king, yet for all his effort he could not protect the earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ śuśrāva rājā sa rākṣasebhyo mahābhayam niryayau nagarāc cāpi caturaṅgabalānvitaḥ
english: Then that king heard of a great peril from the rākṣasas, and went forth from the city attended by his fourfold army.

sanskrit: sa gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ vasiṣṭhāśramam abhyayāt tasya te sainikā rājaṃś cakrus tatrānayān bahūn
english: Having gone a long road, he came upon the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha; and his soldiers, O king, wrought there many wrongs.

sanskrit: tatas tu bhagavān vipro vasiṣṭho ''śramam abhyayāt dadṛśe ca tataḥ sarvaṃ bhajyamānaṃ mahāvanam
english: Then the lordly brahman Vasiṣṭha came to his hermitage and saw the whole great forest being broken to pieces.

sanskrit: tasya kruddho mahārāja vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ sṛjasva śabarān ghorān iti svāṃ gām uvāca ha
english: Wrathful at this, O mighty king, Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages, said to his cow: 'Bring forth dread Śabaras.'

sanskrit: tathoktā sāsṛjad dhenuḥ puruṣān ghoradarśanān te ca tad balam āsādya babhañjuḥ sarvatodiśam
english: Thus bidden, the cow brought forth men of terrible aspect; and they, falling upon that army, scattered it in every direction.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā vidrutaṃ sainyaṃ viśvāmitras tu gādhijaḥ tapaḥ paraṃ manyamānas tapasy eva mano dadhe
english: Seeing his army put to flight, Viśvāmitra the son of Gādhi, deeming penance the higher power, set his mind upon penance alone.

sanskrit: so 'smiṃs tīrthavare rājan sarasvatyāḥ samāhitaḥ niyamaiś copavāsaiś ca karśayan deham ātmanaḥ
english: At this excellent ford of the Sarasvatī, O king, with mind composed, he wasted his own body with vows and fasts.

sanskrit: jalāhāro vāyubhakṣaḥ parṇāhāraś ca so 'bhavat tathā sthaṇḍilaśāyī ca ye cānye niyamāḥ pṛthak
english: He became one who fed on water, who fed on air, who fed on leaves; one who lay upon the bare ground, and observed whatever other separate vows there are.

sanskrit: asakṛt tasya devās tu vratavighnaṃ pracakrire na cāsya niyamād buddhir apayāti mahātmanaḥ
english: Again and again the gods set obstacles to his vow, yet the resolve of that great soul would not turn aside from his observance.

sanskrit: tataḥ pareṇa yatnena taptvā bahuvidhaṃ tapaḥ tejasā bhāskarākāro gādhijaḥ samapadyata
english: Then, having practised manifold penance with the utmost effort, the son of Gādhi grew in splendour like unto the sun.

sanskrit: tapasā tu tathā yuktaṃ viśvāmitraṃ pitāmahaḥ amanyata mahātejā varado varam asya tat
english: Viśvāmitra being thus endowed with penance, the Grandsire of mighty splendour, the giver of boons, deemed him worthy of that boon.

sanskrit: sa tu vavre varaṃ rājan syām ahaṃ brāhmaṇas tv iti tatheti cābravīd brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
english: And he chose his boon, O king, saying: 'May I become a brāhmaṇa'; and Brahmā, the Grandsire of all the worlds, said, 'So be it.'
